results.title: Italy's general strike on Friday to impact transport, schools and hospitals
results.description: CGIL union calls a nationwide walkout over the cost of living and the government’s economic policy, with around 100 demonstrations planned, including a rally in Rome. A general strike called by Italy’s largest trade union, the CGIL, will take place today, Friday 20 November, affecting public and private sectors across the country, including schools, healthcare, public offices and local transport.CGIL, led by general secretary Maurizio Landini, says it is protesting against the rising cost of living and the government’s economic policy. The union opposes increased national spending on rearmament and says too little is being invested in social policy, healthcare and education. Under the slogan “Il futuro è adesso” (The future is now), CGIL has said the government’s budget “accelerates the decline and impoverishment of the country”. Its demands include secure, properly paid and non-precarious work, higher wages and pensions, fairer taxation, a genuinely public health service, the right to education and access to housing. The grassroots union COBAS has also called a general strike for the same day. Public transport The CGIL strike covers buses, trams and metro services for the full 24 hours, though guaranteed service periods will apply, set locally. In Rome, public transport is due to be disrupted between 08.30 and 17.00, and again from 20.00 until the end of service. Other cities have their own timetables:Turin: 09.00 until midday and from 15.00 until the end of serviceGenoa: 09.00 to 17.30 and from 20.30 until the end of serviceBologna: 08.30 to 16.30 and from 19.30 until the end of serviceFlorence: 08.15 to 12.30 and from 14.30 until the end of servicePalermo: 08.30 to 17.30 and from 08.30 until the end of serviceSome local operators, including Milan’s ATM and Naples’ ANM, are not taking part, due to recent strike action. Taxis are also affected for 24 hours, with minimum services guaranteed. There may be delays to ferry services to Italy’s islands, and staff in freight, logistics and motorway and Anas road management are also due to walk out, with essential safety services maintained. Following intervention by the Commission of Guarantee, which oversees strikes in essential services, air and rail transport are exempt from the CGIL strike. However, a separate strike by the unions CUB Trasporti, CAT and SGB, covering rail passengers and freight staff, runs from 21.00 on Friday until 20.00 on Saturday 21 November. Some local public transport companies will also be affected on Saturday. Lists of guaranteed services for Trenitalia, Italo, Trenord and Atac are available on the operators’ websites. Schools and healthcare Friday's strike covers the school and healthcare sectors, as well as public offices, for the whole working day. Disruption is likely to vary by school and hospital, and parents and patients are advised to check with their school or local health authority. Essential and emergency healthcare services are normally guaranteed during strikes. Demonstrations CGIL has organised around 100 demonstrations nationwide. In Rome, the march starts at 09.30 from Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II and will head towards Via dei Fori Imperiali, where Landini is due to give the closing speech in late morning. In Milan, a march leaves Piazza Cadorna at 09.00, while in Bologna the demonstration begins at 09.30 in Piazza dei Martiri. Travellers in Rome should expect road closures and diversions around the march route.

results.title: Iran war costs surpass $48.3 billion; Pentagon yet to assess base damage
results.description: The costs of the Iran war have risen to an estimated USD 48.3 billion as of November 13, but because that total does not include damage to US bases attacked in West Asia, lawmakers are pushing for the Pentagon to provide those figures. Arthur Miller, a Pentagon budget official, provided the latest overall cost estimate on Thursday to the Senate Armed Services Committee, which is considering his nomination to be Navy comptroller. The USD 48 billion figure includes the costs of military operations, as well as for replacing equipment and munitions. Democratic Sen Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut pressed Miller for an estimate on damage to US installations, which Miller said he didn't have. Republican Sen Roger Wicker of Mississippi, the committee's chair, directed Miller to try to provide an answer as soon as possible.
